title: Trapping Rain Water
statement:
Given N non-negative integers representing an elevation map where each bar has width 1, compute how much water can be trapped after raining.

For each position i, the trapped water = min(maxLeft[i], maxRight[i]) - H[i], where maxLeft[i] is the highest bar to the left (including i) and maxRight[i] is the highest bar to the right (including i).

Compute this efficiently in O(N) using prefix max arrays or the two-pointer technique.
inputFormat:
Line 1: a single integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing heights.
outputFormat: A single integer: total units of trapped water.

examples.explanation: Classic example. Water trapped: at indices 2→1, 4→1, 5→2, 6→1, 9→1, total = 6.
Water: 2+4+1+2 = 9. Positions: idx1→2, idx2→4, idx3→1, idx4→2.
